subject: EU audit period, dataflow assurances, and SOC 2 evidence
messages:
From: Helena Bauer <helena.bauer@novafinancial.eu>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: EuroFinTrust Compliance <compliance@eufintrust.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:05:00 +0100
Subject: Request: SOC 2 coverage window + EU hosting evidence

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking this — EuroFinTrust is preparing for our Q1 vendor review. A couple of items we need from Redwood to complete our security sign-off: 

- A copy of your most recent SOC 2 Type II report (we'd like coverage that includes at least through 31 Dec 2026). If the report's audit window does not cover our effective date (we're aiming for 01 Mar 2027), please confirm whether you can provide a bridge letter or an interim attestation and an expected timeline.

- Confirmation of hosting region(s) where customer data at rest is stored for EU customers (we need a short description and evidence — data flow diagram or simple table of which components are in-region).

- Any documentation on cross-border transfer controls (if control plane or backups are outside EU). Examples we commonly accept: bridge letters, dataflow diagrams, SOC2 artifact references, or a CAIQ/SIG summary map.

Attached is a short template showing the fields our procurement team uses to track each item. Could you let us know what you can provide and an expected delivery date?

Thanks,
Helena Bauer
Head of Vendor Risk
Nova Financial / EuroFinTrust

Attachment: SOC2-request-template.pdf (1 page PDF)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Helena Bauer <helena.bauer@novafinancial.eu>
Cc: EuroFinTrust Compliance <compliance@eufintrust.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 coverage window + EU hosting evidence

Hi Helena — thanks for the clear template. Quick answers and next steps below; I'll coordinate the artifacts and timeline with our security and operations teams.

Summary answers:
- SOC 2 Type II: We can provide our 2026 SOC 2 Type II report (audit period: 01 Jul 2025 - 31 Dec 2026). If you need coverage that extends beyond 31 Dec 2026 to 01 Mar 2027, we can supply a signed bridge letter confirming no control changes and an interim controls attestation; target delivery: bridge letter within 5 business days after we finalize language with legal.

- Hosting region: Production customer data for customers who select "EU region" is stored in eu-west-1 (AWS Ireland). Control plane metadata and some analytics telemetry are in our control plane primarily hosted in us-east-1; we have documented controls and encryption-at-rest. We'll provide a compact dataflow diagram and a CSV mapping of services to region.

- Cross-border transfer controls: we will provide the specific policies (encryption, access controls, logging) and references to SOC 2 controls that cover those flows.

Action plan:
1) Kimberly will attach the SOC 2 PDF and a draft bridge letter for your review.
2) Marissa will assemble the EU hosting evidence (dataflow diagram, storage buckets, and retention notes).
3) I'll share a short summary plus a links bundle for your legal and procurement teams.

Target ETA: initial bundle by 2027-01-13 EOD (your timezone) — let me know if you need it sooner.

Attaching our internal FAQ that answers common questions to speed review.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood-SOC2-FAQ.pdf (2 pages)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Kimberly / Marissa — looping you both in to action. Please see Helena's request above and my replies. Concrete asks: 

Kimberly: pull the signed SOC 2 Type II PDF (latest) and prepare a draft bridge letter that can be signed by Legal/Trust. The customer will likely expect the letter to state that no material control changes affecting scope occurred since 31 Dec 2026 and a commitment to provide the next audit timeline.

Marissa: compile a short evidence bundle for EU hosting: 
- One-page dataflow diagram showing eu-west-1 storage and which components (object storage, databases, KV caches) hold customer data at rest.
- A CSV mapping service -> region -> retention period.
- A note on backups and whether any backups are stored outside the EU and the controls (encryption, access).

Please add the filenames to a shared Drive folder and reply-all when the files are ready so I can send to Helena. Target: 2027-01-13 EOD for the bundle.

Thanks — Aditya

Hi Helena — thanks for the patience. Please find the initial package below and a short summary of each item. If you'd like a quick call to walk through anything, I'm available tomorrow morning CET.

Files attached (stubs):
- SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026-12.pdf — Full Type II report (audit window 2025-07-01 to 2026-12-31).
- eu-hosting-artifacts.zip — contains: dataflow_diagram_eu.pdf, service_region_mapping.csv, backup_retention_note.txt, and a checklist of controls.
- bridge_letter_draft.docx — draft bridge letter from Redwood legal (editable).

Short clarifications:
- Audit coverage: the SOC 2 report covers controls through 31 Dec 2026. The draft bridge letter confirms there were no material control changes affecting the scope between 01 Jan 2027 and the present; we can sign that once language is agreed.

- Hosting & cross-border: customer data at rest for EU customers choosing the EU region is stored in eu-west-1 (AWS Ireland). The control plane that orchestrates inference (metadata, telemetry) is hosted in us-east-1; access to customer data is restricted and logged, and network egress is encrypted. Backups for EU-region datasets are also kept in eu-west-1; any cross-region replication (rare) is performed under encryption and with access controls — details included in the eu-hosting-artifacts.zip.

Next steps we propose:
1) You review the draft bridge letter and tell us any required language changes (we can iterate quickly).
2) Once language is agreed, Legal will sign and we will deliver a signed PDF.
3) If you need any additional artifacts (e.g., specific log samples, signed SLA exception), flag them and we'll route through Trust.
